instruction: I have a list of people I owe money to, including amounts and descriptions, in debt_list.csv. For each person, (1) If they have a Venmo account, send the money publicly with the specified amount and description. (2) If not, create an individual (non-grouped) Splitwise expense with the same details so I remember to pay them later. For Splitwise expenses, attach the PDF receipt as well. They are in the same folder as the CSV file.
notes: The CSV contents are unknown at modeling time; the 13-call reference length implies 3 debt entries (each needs a venmo.search_users check plus one settlement call). The model assumes debtor-1 and debtor-2 have Venmo accounts (static (has-venmo-account) facts in :init) and debtor-3 does not; at runtime the branch is decided by the venmo.search_users result (non-empty => create_transaction, empty => record_expense). Knowledge gates: (directory-listed) from file_system.show_directory (recursive=true, reveals the CSV path and the PDF receipts in the same folder), (csv-read) from file_system.show_file, (venmo-status-known ?p) from venmo.search_users. Venmo payments are public (private=false) and paid from Venmo balance (no payment_card_id). Splitwise expenses are non-grouped (no group_id); payer_email is the person owed, debtor_emails is the single-element list with the supervisor's email, and receipt_file_path plus file_system_access_token attach the PDF in the same call. Since quantified goals are disallowed, supervisor-complete-task takes the three distinct debtor records as non-API parameters so its precondition equals the goal conjunction; (debt-settled ?p) is only reachable through the branch consistent with the Venmo-account facts.
